summary:
SpaceSoil is a smart web platform that bridges the gap between NASA’s satellite data and everyday farmers, helping them protect their crops before extreme weather and climate shifts cause real damage. Simply put, farmers usually don’t notice hidden soil moisture loss or crop stress until yields are already suffering, and raw space data is way too complex to interpret on their own.
We solved this by creating an easy-to-use tool where a farmer just enters their land location and crop type, and the system pulls, cleans, and merges data from four NASA sources (MODIS, SMAP, POWER, and GPM) into a clear, map-based dashboard showing soil moisture, rainfall, and crop greenness. Beyond just monitoring current conditions, SpaceSoil compares them against historical patterns to spot unusual anomalies early and send alerts, empowering farmers to make smarter irrigation and field-care decisions before stress turns into loss.
details:
SpaceSoil is a web-based agricultural monitoring and decision-support platform designed to bridge the gap between space-based Earth observation data and everyday farming. It transforms complex satellite datasets into clear, actionable insights to help farmers detect environmental stress early and adapt to unpredictable weather conditions.

The platform operates through a structured, data-driven pipeline:

  1. User Input: Farmers or agricultural specialists enter basic contextual information about their land, including geographic location and selected crop type.
  2. NASA Earth Observation Integration: SpaceSoil retrieves multi-year satellite data (covering December 2019 – December 2025) primarily from NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1.061) for vegetation health (NDVI and EVI), complemented by NASA SMAP (soil moisture) and NASA POWER (agro-climatology).
  3. Data Quality Filtering & Preprocessing: Raw satellite observations are cleaned by inspecting pixel reliability, filtering out cloud-contaminated or unreliable measurements, and handling missing values.
  4. Temporal & Feature Analysis: Using engineered features—such as NDVI Change Rate, EVI Trend, Seasonal Vegetation Patterns, and Vegetation Anomalies—the system tracks multi-year, seasonal, and monthly shifts to flag abnormal crop behavior before visible damage becomes severe.
  5. Accessible Decision Support: Complex metrics are translated into intuitive visualizations and clear risk alerts on a user-friendly web interface without requiring technical expertise.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Early Stress Detection: Identifies subtle vegetation deterioration early, helping farmers respond proactively to droughts, excessive rainfall, or shifting climate patterns.
  • Cost-Effective Wide-Area Monitoring: Replaces expensive, labor-intensive manual field scouting across large agricultural areas with consistent 16-day satellite monitoring.
  • Democratizing Space Data: Makes publicly available NASA datasets understandable and practical for non-technical users, empowering data-driven farming decisions and strengthening local food security.
  • Target Beneficiaries: Designed to support smallholder and commercial farmers, agricultural extension specialists, and environmental researchers.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • NASA Datasets & Portals: NASA MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1.061), NASA SMAP, NASA POWER, NASA Earthdata, AppEEARS, and LP DAAC.
  • Programming & Data Science: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab.
  • Application & Development: Modern Web Technologies (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) for building the interactive, public-facing web interface, alongside AI-assisted tools for code refinement and documentation support.

Creativity & Innovation

Rather than presenting raw, intimidating geospatial rasters or scientific jargon, SpaceSoil acts as a "translation layer" between orbit and field. By combining quality-filtered historical baselines with custom temporal anomaly features (comparing current vegetation behavior against expected seasonal norms), the platform turns passive satellite archives into a practical early-warning companion tailored to a farmer's specific crop context.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Data Reliability & Cloud Interference: Satellite optical data is prone to cloud cover and atmospheric noise; therefore, strict filtering using MODIS Pixel Reliability and VI Quality flags was prioritized before generating any insights.
  • Scientific Transparency & Limitations: Our team explicitly accounted for spatial resolution constraints (250m pixels represent regional trends rather than individual plants) and the 16-day revisit cycle, positioning SpaceSoil as an ethical decision-support tool that complements—rather than replaces—agronomic expertise and laboratory soil testing.
  • Accessibility & Zero-Friction UX: Designed the web platform to be publicly accessible without login barriers or complex setup so farmers can explore environmental indicators effortlessly.
